When the moon's light is overshadowed by the superior light, it seems not to shine; similarly, the ministry of the law, although having received glory from God, seems not to have glory because of the surpassing glory of the gospel ministry; for the lesser always gives way to the greater; if what is being abolished has glory, how much more what remains; the shadow and the law are being abolished, but the ordinances of God remain; the shadow had glory, but the things of Christ have greater glory; having such hope, we use great boldness; the hope of being sufficient ministers of the new covenant, not of the letter, but of the Spirit; it is fitting for such ministers to speak with boldness, not being ashamed of the types, nor of the foolishness of the hearers; for the Holy Spirit, dwelling in the souls of the faithful, makes them understand easily even the deep things; and the disciples of Christ are more glorious, because the word of the gospel has been made clear and simple to them, without anything difficult, unlike the ministry of Moses

For since the sons of Israel were unapproved after so many wonders, Moses put a veil on himself and used veils when speaking the divine law to them, teaching through riddles, so that they could not see the true face of the law, that is, Christ; but in the second, as if they were striking the face, with the shadow having no glory, which shadow and type are also abolished; for the new covenant has been completed, and the end of the abolished law is Christ; therefore, the hidden glory of Moses, Christ, was the end of the abolished law; for if someone removes the shadow and the second face, as if in writing, they will see Emmanuel being formed in many ways on each one, and the one who suffered and saved the world, so that he may be glorified by us and the holy angels worshiping; the light of the Savior's glory is inaccessible to the Jewish minds; since all spiritual contemplation looks towards the mystery of Christ, but the Jewish talents do not approach the faith in him, the veil remains on them, but is abolished in Christ; when they turn to the Lord, the veil will be removed; the Lord himself is the light and reveals the deep and hidden things, and shows the true and glorified face of the law to the wise and sanctified ones in spirit and through faith in Christ

For the law guides to Christ, but the one appointed to guide to something else establishes those being guided not on their own, but rather bears them towards something better and greater than themselves. Hence, the divine Paul says he considers the things in the law as rubbish because of the surpassing knowledge of Christ. The Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom. It is necessary to become spiritual, for it is not possible to see Christ, who is the end of what is being abolished, namely the law. Then, the veil is completely removed, and with unveiled face, they will see the holy Moses, the face or shadow that comes from the letter.
pass_b_english: The glory of the ministry of the law, although it has been overshadowed by the surpassing glory of the gospel, still has a certain glory. However, this glory is not as great as the glory of the gospel, for the lesser always gives way to the greater. If what is being abolished, such as the shadow and the law, has glory, how much more will what remains, the ordinances of God, have glory?

The disciples of Christ have a greater glory, because the word of the gospel has been made clear and simple to them, without anything difficult, unlike the ministry of Moses. Having such hope, we use great boldness, for we are sufficient ministers of the new covenant, not of the letter, but of the Spirit. It is fitting for such ministers to speak with boldness, not being ashamed of the types, nor of the foolishness of the hearers.

The sons of Israel, despite witnessing numerous wonders, proved to be unapproved, and Moses was forced to put a veil on himself when speaking to them about the divine law. This veil was a symbol of the riddles and mysteries that shrouded the true face of the law, which is none other than Christ. The Israelites were unable to gaze upon this glory, and instead, they saw only a faint reflection, a shadow without substance. This shadow, along with the type and figure it represented, has been abolished, for the new covenant has been fulfilled, and Christ is the culmination of the law.

The hidden glory of Moses, which is Christ, was the ultimate goal of the law, and those who remove the veil of the shadow and the second face, as if written in scripture, will behold Emmanuel, who is formed in many ways in each individual, and who suffered and saved the world, enduring the slaughter for the world and rescuing the heavenly. As a result, he will be glorified by us and worshiped by the holy angels. However, the light of the Savior's glory remains inaccessible to the Jewish mind, which is unable to approach the faith in Christ.

The law serves as a guide, leading us to Christ, whereas something else guides us towards what is better and greater than ourselves. This is why the apostle Paul views the things in the law as worthless, considering them rubbish in comparison to the surpassing knowledge of Christ. The Lord is the Spirit, and it is in the Spirit that we find freedom.

To truly see Christ, who is the culmination of what is being abolished - namely, the law - we must become spiritual. Only then can the veil be completely removed, allowing us to see the holy Moses with an unveiled face, the face or shadow that comes from the letter.
